Prevention: Use resistant variety (ADT 39, TRY 3, PY 4 (Jawahar), Moderately resistant (CORH4)
Maintain a spacing of 20 cm x 20 cm (between the rows as well as plant within a row).
Application of potash (5 kg/acre) at tillering stage as additional dose
Irrigation management to reduce humidity as disease is more prevalent under high humidity.
Follow alternate wetting and drying method of irrigation during pannicle iniation and grain formation stage
Monitoring: Rainfall and cloudy weather at flowering and maturity periods induce the disease
Regular observation of panicle from milky stage to maturity stage
Monitoring for the individual rice grain transformed into a mass of yellow fruiting bodies to the size of 1cm.
Common symptoms include the development of yellow smut balls which turn black.
Consider direct control actions as soon as symptoms are found.
Direct Control: Pseudomonas fluorescens at a rate of 10 g (talc) or 2 ml (liquid)/kg of seeds in one litre of water.
P. fluorescens at a rate of 1 kg or 1 litre/acre 3 times at 10 day intervals commencing from 45 days after transplanting.
Seedling root dip for 30 minutes with
P. fluorescens at a rate of 200 ml or 1kg /acre dissolved in 40 litres of water.
P.fluorescens at a rate of 1 kg/acre mixed with 25 kg of decomposed
